data.cultural_impact: The name Hanna has been popular in various cultures, especially in the Christian world. Its significance goes beyond just a beautiful sounding name. It is a name rooted in faith, hope, and perseverance. The story of Hannah from the Old Testament teaches us about the importance of prayer and trust in God. It is a name that carries a message of undying faith and the belief that miracles can happen through God's mercy and grace.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hanna holds profound spiritual significance as it symbolizes the human longing for God's grace and favor. It reminds us of Hannah's unwavering faith and enduring prayer, which ultimately led to the birth of Samuel, a great prophet and leader in Israel. The name Hanna encourages us to trust in God's timing and to never give up on our prayers. It is a name that inspires us to have faith and to believe in the power of God's grace and mercy in our lives.

historical_references.reference: Hannah was the mother of the prophet Samuel. She was a priestess in the tabernacle at Shiloh and was barren. One day, after Elkanah her husband had finished eating and drinking, she went to the tabernacle to pray and wept before the Lord. Eli the priest saw her and thought she was drunk, but Hannah explained her tears were from sorrow and not drink. Hannah made a vow to dedicate her newborn son to the Lord's service if he granted her request for a child. After her prayer, God remembered her and she conceived and gave birth to a son whom she named Samuel. When Samuel was weaned, Hannah fulfilled her vow and brought him to live in the tabernacle under Eli's care.

Hanna, also known as Anne, was a noblewoman in Brittany, France, during the 15th century. She was married to Sir Matthew of Lannoy, who was away for many years due to the Hundred Years' War. During Sir Matthew's absence, Hanna lived as a recluse, devoting herself to prayer and charitable works. She became known for her piety and good works, and pilgrims came from far and wide to seek her counsel and blessings. When Sir Matthew returned, he was so impressed by his wife's transformation that he vowed to live a more devout life.
